title: The Dungeon Dive's 2021 year-end review, Patreon Questions, a look forward to 2022
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7wuBlcFsfvc

The longest and most personal of the year-end videos, structured as review, patron Q&A, look-ahead and awards. The Q&A is where it earns its length.

Asked what it's like running the channel, Daniel (@dungeondive) calculates he earns about ten cents an hour and admits he no longer knows which drives which — whether his love of games sustains the channel or the channel sustains his interest in games. He ranks board games low in his own hobby hierarchy, below books and music, and says he'd give them up first. He is also direct about moderation: the videos drawing the most abuse are his sword and sorcery book videos, which get a fraction of the views, and he defends discussing the misogyny, racism and colonialism in old pulp fiction as encouragement to read it clear-eyed rather than a warning off.

Asked whether the genre has peaked, he says yes — manufacturing and shipping costs are ending the era of huge multi-box Kickstarters, and a big box now brings him more stress than joy. He predicts design will shift as the generation raised on Gloomhaven succeeds the one raised on HeroQuest.

Personal news: after 17 years he is leaving a white-collar job for manual labour and a roughly 50% pay cut. Top five ends with Sleeping Gods, called a masterpiece and his new benchmark for campaign games.

----

Is "past peak dungeon crawl" a prediction about economics or about design?
